summary: Entacapone is a peripherally-acting, reversible COMT inhibitor used only as an adjunct to levodopa/carbidopa to treat Parkinson disease patients experiencing end-of-dose 'wearing-off'. By blocking COMT it reduces peripheral metabolism of levodopa to 3-O-methyldopa, increasing and prolonging plasma levodopa levels and the amount reaching the brain. It is always given with each levodopa dose. Because it enhances dopaminergic effect it can worsen dyskinesia and may require a levodopa dose reduction; it commonly causes diarrhea and harmless brownish-orange urine discoloration.
indications: Adjunct to levodopa/carbidopa to treat patients with idiopathic Parkinson disease who experience end-of-dose 'wearing-off' (signs and symptoms of end-of-dose deterioration)

dosage.d: 200 mg taken together with each dose of levodopa/carbidopa
dosage.t: With each levodopa/carbidopa dose, up to 8 times daily
dosage.n: Max 8 doses (1600 mg)/day; only given concomitantly with levodopa/carbidopa

dosage.d: May need to reduce daily levodopa dose (by lowering dose or extending interval) to manage increased dopaminergic effects
dosage.t: As clinically indicated when starting entacapone
dosage.n: Especially in patients with prior dyskinesia

admin: Give 200 mg with each levodopa/carbidopa dose, up to a maximum of 8 doses per day
May be taken with or without food
Do not abruptly stop or rapidly reduce entacapone (risk of hyperpyrexia and confusion, a neuroleptic-malignant-like syndrome)
Available as a single combination tablet with levodopa/carbidopa (Stalevo) for convenience
moa: Entacapone is a selective, reversible inhibitor of catechol-O-methyltransferase (COMT) in peripheral tissues. When given with levodopa/carbidopa it inhibits the peripheral COMT-mediated metabolism of levodopa to 3-O-methyldopa, increasing the bioavailability and prolonging the elimination half-life of levodopa. This produces more constant plasma levodopa concentrations, increasing the amount of levodopa available to the brain and prolonging its clinical effect.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to entacapone or any excipient
Pheochromocytoma or other catecholamine-secreting tumors (risk of hypertensive crisis)
History of neuroleptic malignant syndrome or non-traumatic rhabdomyolysis
Concomitant use with nonselective MAO inhibitors (and combined MAO-A/MAO-B inhibition)
relative: Concomitant drugs metabolized by COMT or affecting catecholamines
monitor: Dyskinesia and other dopaminergic adverse effects
Signs of liver injury or NMS-like syndrome on withdrawal

preg: There are limited data on use in pregnant women. Entacapone should be used during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: Entacapone is excreted in the milk of lactating animals; it is not known whether it is excreted in human milk. Breastfeeding is not recommended during entacapone treatment, or a decision should be made to discontinue nursing or the drug.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is generally required; entacapone is largely metabolized and eliminated in bile/feces with little renal excretion. Caution is advised in patients undergoing dialysis.
hepatic: Entacapone clearance is reduced in patients with impaired liver function; it should be administered with caution in these patients as plasma levels may be increased.

major: Nonselective MAO inhibitors (and combined MAO-A + MAO-B inhibition) - contraindicated due to impaired catecholamine metabolism

Drugs metabolized by COMT (e.g., isoprenaline/isoproterenol, epinephrine, norepinephrine, dopamine, dobutamine, alpha-methyldopa, apomorphine) - increased heart rate, arrhythmias, blood pressure changes
moderate: Iron salts - entacapone can chelate iron; separate dosing by at least 2-3 hours

Drugs that interfere with biliary excretion, glucuronidation, or intestinal beta-glucuronidase (probenecid, cholestyramine, some antibiotics like erythromycin, rifampicin, ampicillin, chloramphenicol)
Selegiline/rasagiline (selective MAO-B inhibitors) - use with caution
minor: Warfarin (monitor INR; small increases in INR reported)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; separate from iron supplements by 2-3 hours
interactions.diagnostics: Causes reddish-brown discoloration of urine (harmless); may interfere with urine color-based tests

serious: Severe diarrhea with weight loss and dehydration
Neuroleptic-malignant-like syndrome on abrupt withdrawal or dose reduction
rare: Sudden onset of sleep / daytime somnolence
emergency: High fever, muscle rigidity, altered consciousness (NMS-like syndrome)
Signs of rhabdomyolysis (severe muscle pain, dark urine)

monitoring: Dyskinesia and other dopaminergic effects (may need to reduce levodopa)
Bowel habit / persistent diarrhea and weight
Liver function if symptoms of hepatic injury occur
counsel: Take one tablet with each dose of your levodopa/carbidopa medicine
Your urine may turn a harmless brownish-orange color
Diarrhea can occur, sometimes after weeks or months - report persistent diarrhea or weight loss
Do not stop suddenly; speak to your doctor about tapering
Stand up slowly to avoid dizziness; report fainting
Tell your doctor if you notice new urges to gamble, shop, or other impulsive behaviors, or fall asleep suddenly during the day
pk: Prolongs levodopa effect from the first co-administered dose
Peak plasma concentration about 1 hour after an oral dose
Given with each levodopa dose because of its short half-life
Store at room temperature; protect from moisture
pearls: Peripherally acting - it does not cross the blood-brain barrier and works only as a levodopa adjunct, never as monotherapy
Short half-life means it must be dosed with every levodopa dose; the Stalevo combination tablet simplifies this
Diarrhea can appear weeks to months after starting and is the main reason for discontinuation; rule out colitis
Watch for emergence or worsening of dyskinesia early - often requires a levodopa dose reduction
Unlike tolcapone, entacapone is not associated with serious hepatotoxicity and does not require scheduled liver monitoring
missed: If a levodopa/carbidopa dose with its entacapone is missed, take the next scheduled combined dose at the usual time; do not take an extra entacapone tablet alone. Entacapone is only taken together with levodopa/carbidopa.
overdose: Overdose data are limited. The highest entacapone concentrations and overstimulation could cause confusion, decreased activity, and gastrointestinal symptoms. There is no specific antidote; management is supportive with monitoring of cardiovascular status. Because entacapone is highly protein-bound, hemodialysis is unlikely to be beneficial; consider general measures and possible interaction with concomitant levodopa effects.
